hookups.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('Camping is primitive, temporary and dispersed. There are no established campsites and no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations).'), read 2026-10-21

facilities.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ ('no amenities (electric, potable water, dump stations, restrooms, convenience stations)'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Hardware River lists Primitive Camping among its activities; besides the James River boat-ramp lot (where the 300-ft rule bars camping) DWR names upland parking areas on Kidds Mill Road and at the end of Route 611; its page names no camping spot.

booking.source: https://dwr.virginia.gov/camping-on-wmas/ + https://dwr.virginia.gov/wma/hardware-river/ (Recreational Opportunities: 'Primitive Camping'; 'There is ample room for parking near the boat ramp, and other parking areas are located for access to the upland'; 'one parking area is to the left on Kidds Mill Road; another is at the end of route 611'), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed on DWR's Hardware River page that primitive camping is still allowed, and from DWR's statewide camping page: no hookups, no water/dump/restrooms, 14-night limit, $10 camping authorization. Not stated: season, a camping-specific spot on this WMA. Note left as is (the DWR fee line says what the inherited all-in rate cannot).
